'''Producers Midstream Gas Pipeline''' is a natural gas pipeline in the United States, with 3 segments.

==Location==
Residue Header: The pipeline runs from Washita County, Oklahoma to Roberts County, Texas.<ref name="re6804c">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2026-03/CP25-531-000.pdf|title=Order in Palo Duro Transmission L.P. and Palo Duro Pipelines (Texas Gathering), L.P., Docket CP25-531-000, 194 FERC 61,220|website=ferc.gov|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref>
Palo Duro Gas Pipeline: The pipeline runs from Nolan County, Texas to Wheeler County, Texas.<ref name="rb9deb2">{{Cite web|url=https://producersmidstream.com/palo-duro-pipeline-project-notice-of-binding-open-season/#:~:text=The%20proposed%20pipeline%20project%20will%20utilize%20existing|title=https://producersmidstream.com/palo-duro-pipeline-project-notice-of-binding-open-season/#:~:text=The%20proposed%20pipeline%20project%20will%20utilize%20existing|website=producersmidstream.com|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref><ref name="r50f169">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ogj.com/pipelines-transportation/pipelines/article/55300432/producers-midstream-launches-open-season-for-service-on-palo-duro-pipeline|title=https://www.ogj.com/pipelines-transportation/pipelines/article/55300432/producers-midstream-launches-open-season-for-service-on-palo-duro-pipeline|website=ogj.com|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref><ref name="re6804c" />
Palo Duro Lease Agreement Project: The pipeline is proposed to run from Childress County, Texas to Washita County, Oklahoma.<ref name="re6804c" /><ref name="r32f38d">{{Cite web|url=https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2026-00407|title=https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2026-00407|website=federalregister.gov|access-date=2026-11-05}}</ref>

==Background==
===Residue Header===
The Residue Header is part of the Anadarko Gathering System owned by Palo Duro Pipelines (Texas Gathering), L.P., a Producers Midstream company. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission described it as a 150-mile pipeline of 16-inch and 20-inch diameter from Washita County, Oklahoma to Roberts County, Texas.<ref name="re6804c" /> In June 2025, Producers Midstream said its Palo Duro Pipeline would use leased capacity on this header system as part of a new interstate service.<ref name="rbd18b9" /> The commission issued certificates for the project on March 19, 2026.<ref name="re6804c" />

===Palo Duro Gas Pipeline===
The Palo Duro Gas Pipeline is an existing 16-inch pipeline of about 275 miles in Texas, from Nolan County to an interconnection with the header system in Wheeler County.<ref name="re6804c" /> It is operated by Palo Duro Transmission L.P., a Producers Midstream company.<ref name="re6804c" /> In June 2025, Producers Midstream announced plans to convert it to interstate service and began a binding open season.<ref name="rbd18b9" /> On March 19, 2026, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission issued certificates for the project.<ref name="re6804c" /> The commission said the interstate service would use the northernmost 61 miles of the pipeline plus leased header capacity, for up to 80,000 Dth/d.<ref name="re6804c" /> Palo Duro Transmission signed a binding agreement for all of that capacity with Scurry Downstream, LLC.<ref name="re6804c" />

===Palo Duro Lease Agreement Project===
Palo Duro Transmission, working with Producers Midstream, held a binding open season from June 30 to July 14, 2025. Producers Midstream said the project would link Waha residue gas markets in the Permian Basin with Mid-Continent markets in the Anadarko Basin. It targeted industrial, petrochemical, power generation and AI-related behind-the-meter demand.<ref name="rbd18b9" /> East Daley Analytics said it would serve data centers, petrochemical plants and power generators. It said that if fully dedicated to data centers, the line could support 125 to 150 megawatts of load. No new construction is needed, and it connects to Northern Natural, Southern Star, ANR, NGPL, Panhandle Eastern, Enable and Transwestern.<ref name="r728921">{{Cite web|url=https://pgjonline.com/news/2025/july/producers-midstream-to-convert-permian-pipeline-for-interstate-gas-service|title=Producers Midstream to convert Permian pipeline for interstate gas service, Pipeline & Gas Journal, July 21, 2025|website=Pipeline & Gas Journal|access-date=2026-11-04}}</ref>

Palo Duro Transmission signed a binding precedent agreement with Scurry Downstream, an affiliate of Producers Midstream, for all of the capacity. It filed its application on August 1, 2025 and amended it on December 22, 2025. No comments or protests were filed.<ref name="re6804c" /> The project lets Palo Duro Transmission operate the northern 61 miles of the existing pipeline as an interstate line and lease 80,000 Dth/d of capacity on the header pipeline. FERC issued the certificates on March 19, 2026.<ref name="re6804c" />
